title: Deductions & Credits
description: A deduction shrinks income. A credit shrinks the tax. The larger subtraction wins.
wolfLine: A credit is not a deduction with a nicer name.

tax-deduction.definition: An amount that lowers the income the tax is figured on. In a 12% bracket, a $1,000 deduction saves $120. It does not save $1,000.
tax-deduction.example: A $1,000 deduction in the 12% bracket cuts the tax by $120.

tax-credit.definition: An amount that lowers the tax itself, dollar for dollar. A $1,000 credit saves $1,000, up to the rules for that credit.
tax-credit.example: The same $1,000 as a credit saves the whole $1,000, which is $880 more than the deduction.

itemized-deduction.definition: The added-up list of allowed expenses, such as some taxes, mortgage interest, and gifts, used instead of the standard deduction when the list is larger.
itemized-deduction.example: A list that adds to $13,000 loses to the 2026 single standard deduction of $16,100.

steps.title: Dollars off the income, or dollars off the tax
steps.body:
A [[tax deduction]] lowers taxable income. In the 12% bracket, **$1,000** of deduction saves **$120**.

A [[tax credit]] lowers the tax. The same **$1,000** credit saves **$1,000**. The credit saves **$880** more.

steps.prompt: A $1,000 deduction sits in the 12% bracket. How much tax does it save?
A $1,000 credit saves how much tax, before any cap on that credit?
steps.explain: A credit cuts the tax dollar for dollar. $1,000.

steps.prompt: How much more does the credit save than the deduction?
A $1,000 deduction and a $1,000 credit save the same tax in the 12% bracket.
steps.explain: The deduction saves $120. The credit saves $1,000.

lessons.title: The Earned Income Tax Credit
lessons.summary: A maximum is not your credit.

steps.title: 2026, and a warning
steps.body:
For 2026, the maximum [[tax credit|tax-credit]] called the Earned Income Tax Credit is **$8,231** for a taxpayer with three or more qualifying children. Smaller families have smaller maximums. The credit phases out as income rises.

Do not treat $8,231 as the credit for one child, or for every income. The IRS EITC assistant is the way to check a real household.

steps.prompt: What is the 2026 maximum EITC for three or more qualifying children?
steps.explain: $8,231. That maximum is not the amount for one child.

steps.prompt: Jamal has one qualifying child. What is $8,231 to him?
choices: The published maximum for a larger family, not a number this lesson assigns him
steps.explain: One child is not three or more. He uses the IRS assistant.

steps.prompt: Every worker receives the $8,231 maximum in 2026.
steps.explain: The maximum is for a specific family size, and income can phase the credit down to nothing.

steps.prompt: The tool that checks a real EITC amount is the IRS ___ assistant.
steps.explain: EITC assistant. A lesson should not invent the phaseout.

steps.title: Up to $2,200
steps.body:
The [[child tax credit]] is up to **$2,200** per qualifying child for 2026. It starts to shrink above **$200,000** of income, or **$400,000** if married filing jointly.

This page is a single filer under that line, so the full **$2,200** is in play. It is not the Child and Dependent Care Credit, and it is not a dependent-care FSA.

steps.prompt: Tax before the credit is $2,620. What is the tax after this $2,200 credit?
This $2,200 is the medical FSA limit.
steps.explain: The medical FSA is a different account, with a different limit. This line is the child tax credit.

steps.prompt: Whose income, in 2026, is past the start of the phaseout for a single filer?
steps.explain: The shrink starts above $200,000 for a single filer. $40,000 and $85,000 are under it.

lessons.title: Education Credits
lessons.summary: The full American Opportunity amount is $2,500, if you qualify.

steps.title: 2026, Form 8863
steps.body:
The American Opportunity Tax Credit is up to **$2,500** per eligible student: **100%** of the first **$2,000** of qualified expenses and **25%** of the next **$2,000**.

For 2026, the full credit is for modified adjusted gross income of **$80,000** or less if you are single, and it is gone above **$90,000**. Joint filers use **$160,000** and **$180,000**. This lesson does not compute a partial phaseout. The Lifetime Learning Credit is a different credit, up to **$2,000** per return.

steps.prompt: Qualified expenses are $4,000 and you qualify for the full credit. What is 100% of the first $2,000?
steps.explain: The first $2,000 counts in full.

steps.prompt: What is 25% of the next $2,000?
What is the full American Opportunity credit from those two pieces?
A single filer with modified adjusted gross income of $40,000 is over the 2026 line where this credit disappears.
steps.explain: It disappears above $90,000 for a single filer. $40,000 is under the $80,000 line for the full credit.

lessons.title: Refundable or Not
lessons.summary: A credit can stop at the tax, or it can pay you past it.

steps.title: Two endings
steps.body:
A nonrefundable credit can cut the tax to zero and then stop. The leftover does not come back.

Tax of **$400** and a **$1,000** nonrefundable credit uses **$400**. The other **$600** is lost. A refundable credit of **$1,000** against the same **$400** tax can send that **$600** back. The child tax credit is partly refundable. Do not treat every credit as cash.

steps.prompt: Tax is $400 and the nonrefundable credit is $1,000. How much of the credit is used?
steps.explain: It can only erase the $400 of tax.

steps.prompt: How much of that nonrefundable credit does not come back?
The credit is refundable instead. How much can come back after the $400 tax is erased?
Every credit is refundable.
steps.explain: A nonrefundable credit stops at the tax. Read the credit before you count on cash back.

lessons.title: Without Itemizing
lessons.summary: Some subtractions happen before the standard deduction.

steps.title: Adjustments
steps.body:
Some [[tax deduction|tax-deduction]] amounts, often called adjustments, come off income before adjusted gross income. You can take them and still take the [[standard deduction]].

In this example, wages are **$40,000** and a **$1,000** adjustment is allowed. Adjusted gross income is **$39,000**. Taxable income is **$39,000** minus **$16,100**, which is **$22,900**. That is **$1,000** less taxable income than with no adjustment.

steps.prompt: Wages are $40,000 and the adjustment is $1,000. What is adjusted gross income?
What is taxable income after the $16,100 standard deduction?
Without the adjustment, taxable income was $23,900. How much lower is it now?
steps.explain: $23,900 − $22,900 = $1,000. The adjustment and the standard deduction both happened.

steps.prompt: An adjustment means you must itemize.
steps.explain: That is the point of an adjustment. The standard deduction can still come off afterward.

lessons.title: Jamal and the EITC
lessons.summary: His bracket is 10%. The $8,231 figure is not his.

story.title: Jamal checks the EITC
story.body:
Jamal is 29 and a warehouse lead. He is single. His wages are **$28,000**, and he has one qualifying child.

The 2026 standard deduction leaves taxable income of **$11,900**. That is inside the 10% bucket, so the income tax before credits is **$1,190**. A **$1,000** [[tax deduction]] would save him **$100**. A **$1,000** [[tax credit]] would save him **$1,000**.

The **$8,231** EITC maximum is for three or more children. Jamal does not write that number on his return. He uses the IRS EITC assistant.

steps.prompt: What is Jamal’s taxable income?
What is 10% of that $11,900, the tax before credits?
A $1,000 deduction in his 10% bucket saves how much?
What should Jamal do with the EITC?
choices: Claim the $8,231 maximum for three or more children
Skip it because he is in the 10% bracket
steps.explain: One child is not the three-child maximum. The assistant handles the phaseout.

steps.prompt: Jamal’s $11,900 of taxable income has reached the 12% bracket.
steps.explain: The 12% bracket starts above $12,400. He is $500 under that line. $12,400 − $11,900 = $500.

lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: A $2,000 deduction is in the 22% bracket. How much tax does it save?
Itemized deductions in an example are $9,000. The 2026 single standard deduction is $16,100. How much larger is the standard deduction?
The 2026 child tax credit maximum in this course is $2,200 per qualifying child.
steps.explain: That is the 2026 amount, and it shrinks above the income lines you already learned.

steps.prompt: A $500 nonrefundable credit meets a $200 tax. How much of the credit can be refunded?
steps.explain: Nonrefundable means the leftover $300 does not come back. The credit used is $200.
